summary.name: FireHydrant
summary.one_liner: FireHydrant is an incident management platform that combines on-call alerting, automated runbooks, Slack/Teams incident handling, AI-assisted summaries, and post-incident retrospectives.
use_cases: coordinate incident response in Slack or Teams
notify on-call engineers when services break
publish status page updates to stakeholders
run blameless-style retrospectives and track action items
summary.what_it_does: The page describes FireHydrant as an all-in-one incident management product covering on-call, alerting, and response workflows. Automated runbooks codify best practices, and a service catalog shows service ownership and dependencies. Incidents can be managed in Slack or Teams, with AI features that generate incident summaries, status page updates, live transcriptions of Zoom and Google Meet meetings, and triage channels. It also offers AI-enhanced retrospectives, automatic follow-up action items, and analytics for MTTx metrics. For enterprises, the page lists SOC 2 compliance, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and SCIM, plus a public API with 350+ endpoints, Terraform support, and SDKs.
notable: AI-generated incident summaries, status page updates, and live meeting transcriptions
Service catalog with ownership and dependency visibility
350+ API endpoints, Terraform support, and SDKs
Enterprise controls: SOC 2, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, SCIM
caveats: Pricing is not stated on the page; it only claims pricing that fits any team.
Page cites a customer-reported 91% reduction in mean time to mitigate, which is a testimonial-style claim rather than an independent measure.
The listing references Blameless, but the page itself is FireHydrant's marketing page, not a Blameless blog.
